description: Download volume, cache composition and upstream health for the git-pkgs proxy. Accumulated download size is cache hits multiplied by artifact size, in total and per ecosystem.

panels.description: Total bytes served to clients from cache: for each artifact, its size multiplied by the number of times it was served. This is traffic carried, not storage used, so it is normally far larger than the cache on disk. Artifacts evicted from the cache stop contributing.
panels.title: Accumulated download size

panels.description: Bytes the cached artifacts currently occupy in storage — what the cache costs to keep. Not an average, and not the same as accumulated download size, which is what the cache has served.
panels.title: Cache size on disk

panels.description: Accumulated download size divided by the bytes currently cached: how many times over the cache has served what it stores. This is the number that makes the two size figures beside it comparable, and it is the clearest single measure of what the cache is worth.
panels.title: Served per byte cached

panels.description: Number of distinct artifacts held in the cache. A small count with a large accumulated download size just means a few artifacts are being served repeatedly, which is the cache doing its job.
panels.title: Cached artifacts

panels.description: Share of artifact lookups served from cache over the dashboard's time range. Reads as No data when nothing was requested in that range — a range with no traffic has no hit ratio, which is not the same as a hit ratio of zero.
panels.title: Cache hit ratio

panels.description: Accumulated bytes served from cache, per ecosystem, largest first. One measure across categories, so a single hue carries magnitude.
panels.title: Download size by ecosystem

panels.description: How the accumulated total has grown, stacked by ecosystem. A step down means artifacts were evicted, which removes their historical hits from the total.
panels.title: Accumulated download size over time

panels.description: Every per-ecosystem figure the charts leave to a tooltip.
panels.title: Per-ecosystem breakdown

panels.description: Responses per second, by package ecosystem. The ecosystem label on this metric is derived from the request path, so it uses route names (rubygems, packagist, debian, other) rather than the package-ecosystem names the cache metrics use. It is filtered by the Route variable, not Ecosystem.
panels.title: Request rate by route

panels.description: Artifact lookups per second that were served from cache versus fetched upstream.
panels.title: Cache hits and misses

panels.description: 95th percentile time to serve a proxy request, by ecosystem. The ecosystem label on this metric is derived from the request path, so it uses route names (rubygems, packagist, debian, other) rather than the package-ecosystem names the cache metrics use. It is filtered by the Route variable, not Ecosystem.
panels.title: Request duration p95

panels.description: 95th percentile time spent fetching an artifact from the upstream registry, by ecosystem. Only cache misses reach an upstream.
panels.title: Upstream fetch duration p95

panels.description: Upstreams whose artifact-fetch breaker is open. While a breaker is open, cache misses for that host return 502 without contacting the upstream. Alert on this being above zero for more than a few minutes.
panels.title: Circuit breakers open

panels.description: Requests currently in flight.
panels.title: Active requests

panels.description: Circuit breaker trips per upstream registry. A breaker is created per host the proxy fetches artifacts from, and only reports once it has tripped at least once, so an empty panel means no upstream has failed repeatedly.
panels.title: Circuit breaker trips

panels.description: Upstream fetch failures per second, by ecosystem and error type.
panels.title: Upstream errors

panels.description: Storage read/write failures, cached artifacts that failed hash verification on read, and storage health probe failures.
panels.title: Storage and integrity failures

panels.description: 95th percentile storage read/write latency, by operation.
panels.title: Storage operation latency p95

panels.description: Storage operations per second, by operation.
panels.title: Storage operation rate

panels.description: Completed pre-cache scans per second, by scanner. Empty when scanning is not configured.
panels.title: Scan rate by scanner

panels.description: 95th percentile pre-cache scan duration, by scanner. A block-mode scanner's latency is on the critical path of a cache miss.
panels.title: Scan duration p95

panels.description: Artifacts a block-mode scanner refused, and scan calls that failed, timed out or were cancelled. A rising error rate means artifacts are being admitted without a verdict.
panels.title: Artifacts blocked and scan errors

panels.description: Bytes held in the cache per ecosystem. A drop is an eviction sweep.
panels.title: Cache size by ecosystem

panels.description: Artifacts held in the cache per ecosystem.
panels.title: Cached artifacts by ecosystem

panels.description: Package and version rows known per ecosystem. These grow as metadata is fetched, independently of what is cached.
panels.title: Known packages and versions

panels.description: Response body bytes per second written to clients. The ecosystem label on this counter comes from the request path, not the package record, so it is filtered by the Route variable and reports route names (debian, and other for the UI and health checks). Distinct from proxy_downloaded_bytes, which is derived from the database as cache hits times artifact size.
panels.title: Bytes served by route

panels.description: Response bytes per second by client tool, identified from the User-Agent. The label set is closed — an unrecognised User-Agent reports as 'other' — so a caller cannot create new time series. Caller addresses are deliberately not exported as labels; see the access log or the proxy's own analytics page for per-address detail.
panels.title: Bytes served by client

panels.description: Requests per second by client tool. Useful for spotting a runaway CI job or a tool that is not honouring caches.
panels.title: Requests by client

list.description: Route names taken from the request path. These differ from the package-ecosystem names used by the cache metrics.
list.label: Route
list.name: route
